title: Incident: credential containment and provenance notes
content:
Purpose:
This note is an operational runbook for containing exposed credentials, rotating secrets safely, and preserving prosecution-quality evidence. Focus is vaulted secrets (Hashi-style vault + KMS-backed envelopes), RBAC-v2 mapped principals, and reliable SIEM export of audit logs.

Assumptions/context:
- Primary secret store: vault.redwood.internal (HashiCorp Vault-ish; we refer to it as "Vault").
- KMS: cloud-kms (customer master keys for envelope encryption).
- Dedicated HSM-backed emergency escrow (scoped to FOCA/HSM project).
- RBAC v2 is enforced in both Vault and Redwood control plane; mapping between Vault policies and Redwood roles exists in Confluence (see linked_artifacts).
- SIEM: company uses Elasticsearch + Filebeat pipeline; we also export to vendor SIEM for long-term retention.
- This doc is intentionally operational and slightly informal; keep notes for after-action review.

High-level objectives for a suspected key compromise:
1) Contain — prevent further use of the compromised credential(s).
2) Rotate — issue new secrets without disrupting production beyond allowed blast radius.
3) Recover & Validate — ensure legitimate systems resume with rotated creds and collect evidence for investigation.
4) Preserve — copy immutable evidence to SIEM/forensics store (WORM) with clear provenance.

Quick containment checklist (first 30–60 min):
- Identify the credential(s): token id, secret path (vault path), associated principal (user/service), request_id(s) from audit logs.
- Immediately revoke session tokens: `vault token revoke -accessor <accessor>` or revoke lease (service-specific).
- Put Vault path into read-only/freeze: create a deny ACL scoped to path or tag as `frozen:true` if supported.
- Blacklist any API keys at the gateway/proxy level (envoy/ingress) to stop external requests.
- If database credentials are affected: temporarily rotate to a one-time backup user and block old account at the DB network ACL.
- Notify incident@, oncall-sec, and owning service team; open/append to SEC-578 (see linked jira).

Rotation procedure (safe-step sequence):
1) Create replacement secret(s) behind a new version number; prefer immutability: `vault kv put secret/service-x v2=true value=...`
2) Pre-stage rotated secret(s) to a rollout channel that allows canary traffic: update canary config or env var in a dedicated subset (10% traffic).
3) Validate: confirm canary instances succeed for 60–120 min of normal traffic; monitor metrics and alpha logs.
4) Gradual rollout: 10% → 30% → 100% following Redwood rollout cadence; watch for error upticks and latency regressions.
5) Revoke old secret only after confirmation; final step: `vault kv metadata delete secret/service-x <old-version>` if policy allows, otherwise rotate to disabled state and destroy.

RBAC v2 crosswalk (what to check during an incident):
- Map the principal found in Vault audit to Redwood role (control-plane) and cloud identity. Use `rbac-v2-mapper` lookup: principal_id -> [role, groups, policy-set].
- Look for recent role changes around the compromise timestamp (possible privilege escalation). Linked Confluence page stores mapping table.
- If a service account was used, check token minting: which CI system (github actions / gitlab runner /buildkite) minted it? Locate build run IDs.

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields for SIEM export):
- timestamp: ISO8601
- request_id: UUID (unique per API call)
- actor: principal id/email/service account
- actor_origin: IP / region / subnet / entity that initiated request
- action: read/write/delete/lease/revoke/unwrap/rotate
- target_resource: vault path (e.g., secret/services/foo)
- target_type: secret|token|policy|kms_key
- outcome: success|failure|partial
- response_code: numeric/http code
- kv_meta: {version, lease_id} (flatten as kv_version, lease_id)
- evidence_ref: pointer to archived payload/snapshot id (if captured)
- governance_tags: [rbac_role, environment, sensitivity] (flatten to comma list)

SIEM/export notes and example pipeline filters:
- We ship Vault audit log JSON files to filebeat which tags them with `log_source=vault` and `env=prod`.
- Minimal filtering/transforms should be done at ingestion — preserve raw event to S3/long-term store first.
- Example jq pipeline to normalize fields before ES ingest:
  cat vault-audit.log | jq '{timestamp:.time, request_id:.request_id, actor:.auth.client_token_accessor, action:.request.operation, target_resource:.request.path, outcome:(.response==null?"failure":"success"), raw:.}'
- Map `kv_version` -> numeric field for queries; map `rbac_role` to text for downstream dashboards.

Evidence automation (scripts & what to capture):
- For every suspected compromise capture: full vault-audit events for +/- 24h around the event, snapshots of the vault path metadata, KMS access logs (cloud-kms), cloud IAM audit for role bindings, container host logs, and proxy logs.
- Automated collector (repo: tools/siem-exporter): runs `vault audit list` and `vault read sys/logs` + cloud-gcloud/az cli to pull KMS IAM change events. Output to `evidence-archive/<incident-id>/raw/` and then to WORM S3 bucket `s3://sec-evidence-worm/<incident-id>/`.
- Evidence integrity: hash each artifact (sha256) and store manifests in `manifest.json` and in SIEM event evidence_ref. Use HMAC with escrow key stored in HSM.

Break-glass / emergency escrow flow (controlled override):
- Purpose: grant temporary access to a sealed store when normal RBAC/rotation would take too long and business continuity is in danger.
- Preconditions: CEO/Security director approval + ticket in SEC-578 with signed justification; Ops lead and 2nd approver in Slack thread #sec-breakglass.
- Steps:
  1) Create temporary role in Vault with TTL 1h, strongly-scoped path. `vault write auth/token/roles/eg-<incident> ...`
  2) Mint ephemeral token and record accessor; store token encrypted in HSM escrow and log to SIEM with `action=break_glass`.
  3) Use token strictly for containment tasks only; rotate immediately after use and destroy token accessor.
- Post-incident audit: Every break-glass action must be logged, backed up to WORM, and reviewed by SecOps within 72 hours.

Credential inventory reconciliation notes (spreadsheet columns):
- id (unique), secret_path, owning_team, owner_oncall, principal_type (service/user), provisioned_by (CI/tool), last_rotation_date, rotation_policy, kms_key_id, exposure_flag (yes/no), last_access_log (timestamp), linked_tickets (list), remediation_status (open/in-progress/done), notes
- Reconciliation process: weekly automated scan vs inventory; exceptions report emailed to owning_team@. CSV exports live in `s3://sec-inventory/daily/` and are compared to vault-engineered list.

Known gaps / TO-DOs / unresolved:
- Need better canonical mapping between Vault lease IDs and Redwood request_ids for full provenance. Current mapping requires cross-correlation using time windows which is fragile.
- Make proof-of-proof (signed manifests) routine part of collector; currently semi-manual.
- Add an explicit automated play that, given a compromised secret path, creates rotated secret, updates service config via templater, and can roll back if errors exceed threshold. (See infra ticket: SEC-592).

Quick commands reference (ops):
- Revoke token: `vault token revoke -accessor <accessor>`
- Freeze path (policy workaround): `vault policy write freeze-policy - <<EOF path "secret/data/service-x" { capabilities = ["deny"] } EOF` then attach to principal.
- Export audit segment: `jq 'select(.time>="2026-02-27T00:00:00Z" and .time<="2026-02-27T04:00:00Z")' /var/log/vault/audit.log > /tmp/incident-audit.json`

Postmortem checklist (after incident closure):
- Confirm old secrets are destroyed/disabled and there are no lingering credentials.
- Ensure all evidence is preserved and manifests stored in WORM.
- Update inventory and RBAC mapping if it contributed to the incident.
- Produce a short exec summary: impact, root cause hypothesis, remediation, and preventative controls (email to execs + postmortem doc).

Notes to self: keep this document loose — many teams prefer one-page TL;DRs. Convert to PDF with annotated timeline for SEC-578 when we finalize.

Appendix: useful links and scripts
- tools/siem-exporter (github): github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tools/siem-exporter
- RBAC v2 mapping confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+V2+Mapping
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-578

End of document.
